purpose: Machine-readable rule-specification foundation for CiteJury. EP-033 narrows Indian judgment support around verified/scoped rules instead of broad plausible formatting.

rules.label: Supreme Court of India neutral citation
validation: sequence number must contain digits only
court, if supplied, must identify Supreme Court of India
formatting: token is year + INSC + sequence number with no inserted spaces
full output is case name, token
limitations: Does not verify that the sequence number belongs to the entered case
Does not cover High Court neutral citations
Does not add parallel citations or pinpoints
rules.nextEp: EP-036 for larger browser-only citation corpus

rules.label: Readable Indian judgment citation helper
validation: year must be four digits when supplied
limitations: Readable helper only; prefer the narrower SCI neutral, SCC, or AIR rules when applicable
Reporter-specific editorial requirements still require manual verification

rules.label: SCC law-report judgment citation scoped helper
limitations: Common core pattern only: case name, (year) volume SCC first page
Does not verify party names, parallel citations, pinpoints, supplement reports, or editorial variants
rules.nextEp: EP-036 for larger browser-only citation corpus

rules.label: AIR law-report judgment citation scoped helper
limitations: Common core pattern only: case name, AIR year court first page
Does not verify regional variations, parallel citations, pinpoints, or party names
rules.nextEp: EP-036 for larger browser-only citation corpus

rules.label: OSCOLA-like judgment helper
validation: year must be four digits when supplied
limitations: Existing output is OSCOLA-like, not a complete OSCOLA implementation.
EP-034 should implement neutral citation, law report priority, legislation, secondary sources, and bibliography behavior with tests.

rules.label: Readable legislation citation helper
validation: year must be four digits when supplied
limitations: Provision labels, chapter numbers, enactment numbers, jurisdiction, and amendments require future rule expansion.
